definition: Cross-lingual Language Model — Meta’s pretrained multilingual LM line that learns shared representations across 100+ languages.
details: Cross-lingual Language Model — Meta’s pretrained multilingual LM line that learns shared representations across 100+ languages.

explainer.lead: XLM, or Cross-lingual Language Model, is Meta's line of pretrained multilingual language models that learns shared representations across more than 100 languages. It matters because one model can serve many languages, including low-resource ones.

tiers.eli5: It is a translator-in-training that reads many languages and learns what they have in common, instead of studying each one separately.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for cross-lingual transfer, so a task trained in one language can be applied to others. The pitfall is uneven quality, with less-resourced languages typically performing worse.
tiers.paperLevel: A pretrained multilingual language model learning shared representations across over 100 languages. Its limits follow from data imbalance: languages with less training text get weaker representations.

explainer.example: A model fine-tuned on English sentiment data is applied to French reviews through its shared cross-lingual representations rather than French training data.
